concepts.label: program_text

concepts.label: class_declaration
concepts.description: public class Name { ... } -- the outer container

concepts.label: main_method
concepts.description: public static void main(String[] args) -- entry point

concepts.label: statement
concepts.description: one step, terminated by ;, executed in sequence

concepts.label: block
concepts.description: { ... } grouping statements

concepts.label: print
concepts.description: System.out.print -- output with no newline

concepts.label: println
concepts.description: System.out.println -- output with a trailing newline

concepts.label: string_literal
concepts.description: "Hello, World" -- the text being printed

concepts.label: compile
concepts.description: javac turns source into bytecode

concepts.label: run
concepts.description: java executes main in the JVM

concepts.label: literal
concepts.description: a constant value written in code (42, 3.14, true, 'a', "hi")

concepts.label: primitive_type
concepts.description: int, double, boolean, char

concepts.label: int
concepts.description: 32-bit integer primitive

concepts.label: double
concepts.description: 64-bit floating-point primitive

concepts.label: boolean
concepts.description: true/false primitive

concepts.label: char
concepts.description: 16-bit character primitive

concepts.label: variable
concepts.description: a named, typed box that holds a value

concepts.label: assignment
concepts.description: = stores the computed value of the right side

concepts.label: expression
concepts.description: anything that evaluates to a value

concepts.label: integer_division
concepts.description: / on two ints truncates; % is the remainder

concepts.label: operator_precedence
concepts.description: the order operators bind in an expression

concepts.label: type_conversion
concepts.description: implicit widening and explicit (cast)

concepts.label: string_type
concepts.description: String -- a reference type, not a primitive

concepts.label: string_concatenation
concepts.description: + with a String builds a new string

concepts.label: boolean_expression
concepts.description: an expression that evaluates to true/false

concepts.label: relational_operators
concepts.description: < > <= >= == != producing a boolean

concepts.label: short_circuit
concepts.description: &&/|| stop evaluating once the result is known

concepts.label: if_statement
concepts.description: run a block only when the condition holds

concepts.label: if_else_statement
concepts.description: choose one of two blocks

concepts.label: nested_conditionals
concepts.description: else-if chains and conditionals inside conditionals

concepts.label: while_loop
concepts.description: repeat a block while a condition holds

concepts.label: for_loop
concepts.description: a while with init/condition/update packaged together

concepts.label: loop_control
concepts.description: the three slots: init ; condition ; update

concepts.label: loop_variable
concepts.description: the counter that drives the loop

concepts.label: loop_body
concepts.description: the block repeated each pass

concepts.label: accumulator_pattern
concepts.description: building up a running total/result

concepts.label: counter_pattern
concepts.description: counting occurrences across passes

concepts.label: nested_loops
concepts.description: a loop inside a loop

concepts.label: loop_scope
concepts.description: lifetime/scope of variables in/around the loop

concepts.label: array_declaration
concepts.description: int[] a; -- declares an array variable

concepts.label: array_creation
concepts.description: new int[n] -- allocates n slots

concepts.label: array_default_values
concepts.description: new slots start at 0 / false / null

concepts.label: array_initializer
concepts.description: {1, 2, 3} literal initialization

concepts.label: indexing
concepts.description: a[i] -- 0-based access

concepts.label: length_field
concepts.description: a.length is a field, not a method

concepts.label: array_bounds
concepts.description: valid indices are 0 .. length-1; otherwise throws

concepts.label: array_traversal
concepts.description: walking the array with an index loop

concepts.label: enhanced_for
concepts.description: for (int x : a) -- the for-each form

concepts.label: array_aliasing
concepts.description: two variables can refer to the same array

concepts.label: two_dimensional_array
concepts.description: an array of arrays (a[i][j])

concepts.label: command_line_args
concepts.description: args[] -- strings passed at launch

concepts.label: parsing
concepts.description: Integer.parseInt / Double.parseDouble turn text into numbers

concepts.label: standard_output
concepts.description: StdOut / System.out

concepts.label: standard_input
concepts.description: StdIn -- reading a stream of values

concepts.label: standard_drawing
concepts.description: StdDraw -- graphical output (book-specific)

concepts.label: stream_model
concepts.description: input and output as sequential streams

concepts.label: read_loop_idiom
concepts.description: reading until end-of-input

concepts.label: redirection
concepts.description: < / > send a file in/out as standard input/output

concepts.label: piping
concepts.description: | connects one program's output to another's input

concepts.label: input_graph
concepts.description: read the page links from input

concepts.description: a 2-D array of move probabilities (rows sum to 1)

concepts.description: pick the next page from a cumulative-probability test

concepts.description: take many random steps

concepts.description: tally visits to estimate page rank

misconceptions.label: ParenthesesOnlyIfArgument
misconceptions.wrong_belief: () are optional on a no-argument call like println

misconceptions.label: PrintEqualsPrintln
misconceptions.wrong_belief: print and println behave the same (no newline difference)

misconceptions.label: ClassNameMatchesFile
misconceptions.wrong_belief: class name and filename are independent

misconceptions.label: StatementNeedsNoTerminator
misconceptions.wrong_belief: a statement runs without the ;

misconceptions.label: CompileRunsProgram
misconceptions.wrong_belief: compiling also executes the program

misconceptions.label: VariablesHoldExpressions
misconceptions.wrong_belief: = stores the expression itself, not its computed value

misconceptions.label: AssignCompares
misconceptions.wrong_belief: = compares two values instead of assigning

misconceptions.label: AssignmentNotExpression
misconceptions.wrong_belief: an assignment cannot be used inside a larger expression

misconceptions.label: LocalVariablesAutoInitialized
misconceptions.wrong_belief: local variables get a default value on their own

misconceptions.label: NoReservedWords
misconceptions.wrong_belief: keywords may be reused as identifiers

misconceptions.label: NoAtomicExpression
misconceptions.wrong_belief: a single literal or variable "isn't an expression"

misconceptions.label: OutsideInMethodNesting
misconceptions.wrong_belief: nested calls run outside-in, not arguments-first

misconceptions.label: ArithmeticPlusPrecedes
misconceptions.wrong_belief: arithmetic + binds tighter than string-concatenation +

misconceptions.label: StringPlusStringifiesExpression
misconceptions.wrong_belief: + with a String turns the whole other side into a string first

misconceptions.label: CharNotNumeric
misconceptions.wrong_belief: char is not a numeric type

misconceptions.label: LargeIntegerLong
misconceptions.wrong_belief: a large integer literal is automatically long

misconceptions.label: NoFloatLiterals
misconceptions.wrong_belief: Java has no float literals

misconceptions.label: NoLongLiterals
misconceptions.wrong_belief: Java has no long literals

misconceptions.label: StringLiteralNoObject
misconceptions.wrong_belief: a string literal isn't a String object until the constructor is called

misconceptions.label: VariablesHoldObjects
misconceptions.wrong_belief: a reference variable holds the whole object, not a reference

misconceptions.label: AssignmentCopiesObject
misconceptions.wrong_belief: assigning a reference copies the object

misconceptions.label: EqualityOperatorComparesObjectsValues
misconceptions.wrong_belief: == compares contents (the String == bug)

misconceptions.label: EqualsComparesReferences
misconceptions.wrong_belief: .equals() compares references, not contents

misconceptions.label: NullIsObject
misconceptions.wrong_belief: null is an object

misconceptions.label: ObjectsMustBeNamed
misconceptions.wrong_belief: you need a variable to create an object

misconceptions.label: ComparisonWithBooleanLiteral
misconceptions.wrong_belief: you must write == true / == false to test a boolean

misconceptions.label: MapToBooleanWithIf
misconceptions.wrong_belief: you need an if to turn a boolean expression into a boolean

misconceptions.label: MapToBooleanWithConditionalOperator
misconceptions.wrong_belief: you need ? : to do the same

misconceptions.label: ConditionalIsSequence
misconceptions.wrong_belief: if-else is the same as two separate ifs

misconceptions.label: IfIsLoop
misconceptions.wrong_belief: an if body repeats while its condition holds

misconceptions.label: NoShortCircuit
misconceptions.wrong_belief: logical AND/OR always evaluate both sides (Java short-circuits them)

misconceptions.label: NoSingleLogicAnd
misconceptions.wrong_belief: & is only a bitwise operator

misconceptions.label: PreIncrementBeforeLoop
misconceptions.wrong_belief: ++i in the for-update runs before the body each pass

misconceptions.label: LoopBodyScopeImpliesLoopLifetime
misconceptions.wrong_belief: a variable declared in the loop body lives across all iterations

misconceptions.label: LoopVariableLifetimeScope
misconceptions.wrong_belief: confusions about the loop variable's lifetime and scope

misconceptions.label: ForVariableScopeBeyondLoop
misconceptions.wrong_belief: confusions about the loop variable's lifetime and scope

misconceptions.label: InfiniteLoopUnnoticed
misconceptions.wrong_belief: a condition that never goes false still terminates

misconceptions.label: OffByOneBound
misconceptions.wrong_belief: < vs <= and 0..n vs 0..n-1 are interchangeable

misconceptions.label: ArrayHasLengthMethod
misconceptions.wrong_belief: you call length() instead of using the length field

misconceptions.label: ArraysGrow
misconceptions.wrong_belief: an array grows as you add elements

misconceptions.label: ArrayInitializerContentsInBrackets
misconceptions.wrong_belief: initializer values go in [] instead of {}

misconceptions.label: ForEachIteratesOverIndices
misconceptions.wrong_belief: a for-each loops over indices, not values

misconceptions.label: ForEachVariableIsElement
misconceptions.wrong_belief: assigning the for-each variable writes back into the array

misconceptions.label: OutOfBoundsElementsAreNull
misconceptions.wrong_belief: an out-of-bounds read returns null (it throws)

misconceptions.label: MultidimensionalArray
misconceptions.wrong_belief: a 2-D array is one thing, not an array of arrays

misconceptions.label: NoJaggedArrays
misconceptions.wrong_belief: multi-dimensional arrays must be rectangular

misconceptions.label: OnlyInnermostArrayElements
misconceptions.wrong_belief: only the innermost elements are accessible

misconceptions.label: ArrayListIsArray
misconceptions.wrong_belief: an ArrayList is an array (borderline; beyond Chapter 1 CS1)

misconceptions.label: ArgsAreNumbers
misconceptions.wrong_belief: command-line args arrive already typed, no parsing needed

misconceptions.label: RedirectionIsArgument
misconceptions.wrong_belief: a redirected file shows up in args[]

misconceptions.label: CumulativeOffByOne
misconceptions.wrong_belief: the cumulative-probability boundary test is inclusive/exclusive interchangeably

misconceptions.label: IntegerProbability
misconceptions.wrong_belief: probabilities computed with integer division stay correct

misconceptions.label: EvaluationResultsArePrinted
misconceptions.wrong_belief: Evaluating an expression means outputting its result

misconceptions.label: ToStringPrints
misconceptions.wrong_belief: Invoking toString() prints something

misconceptions.label: FinalReferenceImpliesImmutability
misconceptions.wrong_belief: An object referred to by a final variable is an immutable object

misconceptions.label: NoCharEscape
misconceptions.wrong_belief: \ is a normal character in char and String literals

misconceptions.label: SingleQuoteString
misconceptions.wrong_belief: String literals can be in single quotes

misconceptions.label: LiteralString
misconceptions.wrong_belief: When passing a literal string as argument to a method, no quotes are needed

misconceptions.label: LiteralNoExpression
misconceptions.wrong_belief: A literal is not an expression

misconceptions.label: IntegerDivisionToRational
misconceptions.wrong_belief: Dividing two integers can produce a rational number

misconceptions.label: NoImplicitWidening
misconceptions.wrong_belief: Smaller types are never automatically converted into bigger ones without an explicit cast

misconceptions.label: NoCastIfSameSize
misconceptions.wrong_belief: If a variable is at least as big (bit-width) as a value, then no cast is needed to a assign the value to the variable

misconceptions.label: NumericToBooleanCoercion
misconceptions.wrong_belief: Numeric types can be coerced to boolean

misconceptions.label: PrimitiveVariablesDynamicallyTyped
misconceptions.wrong_belief: The type of a primitive variable depends on its value

misconceptions.label: ExpressionsDynamicallyTyped
misconceptions.wrong_belief: One has to evaluate an expression to determine its type

misconceptions.label: CompositeExpressionsUntyped
misconceptions.wrong_belief: Expressions that consist of multiple parts have no type

misconceptions.label: UntypedVariables
misconceptions.wrong_belief: Variable declarations don't need a type

misconceptions.label: UndeclaredVariables
misconceptions.wrong_belief: Variables can be used even without being declared beforehand

misconceptions.label: NoLocalVariables
misconceptions.wrong_belief: There are no local variables

misconceptions.label: MultiValueVariable
misconceptions.wrong_belief: A variable can contain more than one value

misconceptions.label: ExpressionAssigns
misconceptions.wrong_belief: An expression that reads a variable also updates its value after the evaluation

misconceptions.label: TargetTyping
misconceptions.wrong_belief: The type of a numerical expression depends on the type expected by the surrounding context

misconceptions.label: RationalLiterals
misconceptions.wrong_belief: Rational fractions are literals

misconceptions.label: ZeroDigitsCompress
misconceptions.wrong_belief: In integer numbers, decimal digits with value `0` take less storage than decimal digits with other values

misconceptions.label: NoStringToString
misconceptions.wrong_belief: One cannot invoke toString() on a String

misconceptions.label: StringRepetitionOperator
misconceptions.wrong_belief: The multiplication operator can repeat a String a number of times

misconceptions.label: IfRequiresElse
misconceptions.wrong_belief: Every if statement requires an else

misconceptions.label: ElseAlwaysExecutes
misconceptions.wrong_belief: The else branch of an if-else statement always executes

misconceptions.label: ElsIf
misconceptions.wrong_belief: There is an elsif keyword for multi-way conditional statements

misconceptions.label: ForIsConditional
misconceptions.wrong_belief: The body of a for statement executes at most once

misconceptions.label: LoopTerminatingCondition
misconceptions.wrong_belief: For and while loops end when the condition becomes true

misconceptions.label: ArrayAccessWithParentheses
misconceptions.wrong_belief: Parentheses are used to access an element in an array

misconceptions.label: ArrayAllocationWithoutNew
misconceptions.wrong_belief: Arrays are created without the new keyword

misconceptions.label: ArrayBracketCountIsLength
misconceptions.wrong_belief: The number of brackets in an array type or an array initializer corresponds to the length of the array

misconceptions.label: ArrayElementsUntyped
misconceptions.wrong_belief: Elements of arrays are untyped

misconceptions.label: ArrayElementTypeRepeats
misconceptions.wrong_belief: The type of a multi-dimensional array is written as T[] T[] T[]

misconceptions.label: ArrayLengthCannotBeZero
misconceptions.wrong_belief: An array cannot have a length of 0 elements

misconceptions.label: ArrayLengthPartOfType
misconceptions.wrong_belief: The length of an array is part of its type

misconceptions.label: ArrayRankIsLength
misconceptions.wrong_belief: Array rank and array length are the same thing

misconceptions.label: ArrayRankNotPartOfType
misconceptions.wrong_belief: The rank of an array is not part of its type
